_how: Top level: rubric_locked_at and scoring_guide_sha256, written by build_briefs.py --lock-guide before the first submission arrives. Then one object per finalist slug. Claude writes received (the date the work came; a file of any name in challenge/submissions/ also counts), summary, what_came, track, clarifying_questions (every question the finalist asked, with the date and the answer you gave; [] when none), assumptions_stated (their own words; [] when none) and the claude block, each note against SCORING-GUIDE.md with a quote. YOU write the founder block first, here or on REVIEW.html: four questions per part, each [score 1 to 5, one line of evidence]. Claude's notes for a part are hidden on the page until your four ratings for that part are in. Parts: core (the shared task, the fair comparison) and specialist (judged against its own track, not compared across tracks). walkthrough: one decision from the submission and the three short questions, with your notes. decision: open / hire for this role / runner-up / no, close with thanks. internal_note: anything the candidate must not hear.

first-last.what_came: A two-page document and one spreadsheet tab
first-last.summary: Two or three sentences: what the submission does, in plain words.

clarifying_questions.question: Their question, word for word
clarifying_questions.about: which missing information it was about

assumptions_stated: Their stated reading of an open point, quoted

understood_goal: note with a quote from the submission

claude.read: Three or four sentences: the strongest point, the clearest gap, what it says about the work in this role.

walkthrough.decision: The one choice from the submission you ask about
questions: Walk me through this one choice.
What would you change with another hour?
walkthrough.held: What held up when they explained it, and what did not.
